refuted_border_padding_mechanism.claim: padding_mode=border charges out-of-box vertices the boundary value, so an episode leaving the SDF box reads as catastrophic penetration
refuted_border_padding_mechanism.why: normalising all three axes by extents.max()/2 makes the grid a CUBE of side extents.max() while the room occupies only its own bbox, so the measured floor-to-grid margin is 2.0-6.6 m, not the 12 cm inferred from the mesh bbox

protocol.strata: by frame-count VALUE, ties never split

by_rank_quartile_SUPERSEDED.reason: only ten distinct frame counts exist (42*seg_len+6, seg_len 2..11) and every quartile boundary lands on a heavily populated value (109 episodes at exactly 132), so a rank split cuts a tie group arbitrarily and the cut depends on the sort algorithm; two runs disagreed on the quartile medians and tail-member counts

conclusions: The penetration tail has two independent causes: scene identity (R^2 0.271, unchanged at 0.274 after removing a cubic in log frames) and sequence length (R^2 0.091 after removing scene means; within-scene rho +0.298, positive in 52 of 67 scenes, sign test p 6.5e-06).
Object identity is NOT a cause (R^2 0.019). The P2-BG closure recommendation of ObjectConditionedGate for the penetration mass is withdrawn.
The border-padding mechanism asserted in the 2026-08-31 preregistration is REFUTED: six null rank correlations against scene box geometry. The tail depth is real geometry.

P2-BG geometric gains decay with rollout length while the contact cost RISES monotonically. By frame-count value: frame_ratio -24.1/-27.2/-21.2/-10.1%, contact -12.0/-11.5/-14.6/-16.3% (all eight significant), feet_height -7.6/-9.3/-5.5(null)/-4.0(null)%. S4 is 39 episodes holding 12 of the 47 tail episodes, a 3.7x enrichment.

Two effects are visible only stratified: foot_sliding on the longest episodes flips sign to +64.1% (null, n=39, baseline 0.0898 vs ~0.18 elsewhere), and scene_obj_penetration_s_mean is +15.5% SIGNIFICANTLY WORSE on S2 (CI [+0.32,+9.96], n=159) while the overall row is a +2.1% null.
Stratify by frame-count VALUE, never by rank: only ten distinct counts exist and every rank quartile boundary cuts a tie group, so the split is not reproducible across sort algorithms.
Therefore: report every mixer row length-stratified, and treat the tail as needing a window-boundary mechanism rather than a better per-step blend.
